A/B comparison workflows and canary gating
Console UI for evals and Optimize recommendations
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Liam Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (Redwood CSM), Jared Lowe (Head of ML, Acumen), Marisol Vega (Director Product), Ethan Chu (SRE), Sofia Ramierez (Data Scientist)

00:00 Liam Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intro. I'm Liam from Redwood, joining with Priya our solutions engineer and Asha who will help run onboarding.
00:18 Jared Lowe: Yep thanks Liam, quick note we got about 45 minutes, we want to see how Redwood handles evals, specifically prompt sets and regression alerts — last thing we had was a bad rollout that regressed ordering relevance so we want automated detection.
00:30 Priya Shah: Great, we'll demo the Console evals flow, the API for programmatic checks, and Optimize recommendations. We'll start with how you define a prompt set and label expectations, then show regression alerts and A/B comparisons.
00:45 Marisol Vega: Also want to understand false positives — we get lots of noise when thresholds are naive.
00:55 Priya Shah: Totally, we'll cover threshold tuning, anomaly scoring, and human-in-the-loop review hooks.
01:10 Asha Patel: Quick logistical note: we'll share the deck and a pilot runbook after.
01:20 Sofia Ramierez: We already pulled a sample of prompts and labelled expected intents, will upload during pilot.
01:28 Priya Shah: Awesome, show of the Console: (screen share) — top-left is Eval -> Prompt Sets. You can import CSV or connect to S3. You define input, expected output, metric (accuracy, BLEU, rank@k).
01:50 Priya Shah: For written responses, we support many metrics and custom scoring functions via a lightweight lambda hook — some customers plug in their own rubric.
02:10 Jared Lowe: That lambda hook, is it running in our env or Redwood's? We have data sensitivity concerns.
02:20 Priya Shah: You can host scoring hooks in your VPC or run them in Redwood with encryption; for pilot we recommend VPC-hosted scoring for sensitive labels. There was a slight hiccup on some transcriptions, sorry — I mean the scoring runs can be configured.
02:40 Ethan Chu: If we host scoring in VPC, what networking do you require? We use private peering.
02:50 Priya Shah: We support VPC peering and private link connectors; we'll capture network contacts as an action item.
03:10 Priya Shah: Back to the UI — you can tag prompt sets by product area, add metadata like schema version and owner. Then you can schedule baseline runs daily or on rollout.
03:35 Marisol Vega: When you say baseline run, do you compute statistical significance for A/B?
03:45 Priya Shah: Yes, we provide A/B comparison widgets with p-values and effect size, and you can set automatic gate rules — if metric delta crosses threshold, the canary rollbacks or triggers manual review.
04:10 Jared Lowe: How do you handle non-deterministic LLM outputs?
04:18 Priya Shah: We run multiple seeds, aggregate via median scores, and support rank-based metrics for retrieval tasks. Also support embedding similarity thresholds for rerankers.
04:40 Sofia Ramierez: Any support for adversarial or stress prompts? We have a corpus of edge cases.
04:48 Priya Shah: Yes you can mark those as 'stress' prompt sets and get separate alerting sensitivity.
05:00 Liam Carter: Quick pause — Marisol you mentioned false positives; wanted to highlight the regression alert pipeline: we do rolling windows, outlier detection, and can fuse signal from multiple metrics to reduce noise. You can also tune the alerting sensitivity per prompt set.
05:28 Marisol Vega: Ok good. Can we map alerts to Slack and PagerDuty?
05:34 Priya Shah: Yes, native integrations with Slack and PagerDuty; alerts include context and deep link to the Console with failing examples.
05:48 Ethan Chu: What about rate and cost when running daily baselines — say we have 50k prompts?
05:58 Priya Shah: We recommend sampling and stratified sampling; Optimize can suggest batching/quantization profiles to keep cost down. Pilot runs usually start with a representative subset, then scale.
06:30 Jared Lowe: For canary gating, does Redwood hook into our CI/CD?
06:38 Priya Shah: We provide an API endpoint for eval results and a webhook to your CI, plus a CLI that returns pass/fail to be used by pipelines.
06:50 Sofia Ramierez: About A/B, can we compare model variants including quantized versions?
06:56 Priya Shah: Yes, we can compare model variants and maintain mapping between model id and quantization profile, so you can see both quality delta and cost delta.
07:20 Marisol Vega: How does historical drift detection work?
07:28 Priya Shah: It tracks metric trends, embedding distribution drift via MMD and centroid shift, and will surface dataset shift alerts. We also support manual tagging of cohorts to track per-cohort regressions.
07:45 Jared Lowe: We'd like cohort tracking by geography and user segment.
07:50 Priya Shah: That's supported — tag prompts with metadata and you can visualize breakdowns.
08:05 Liam Carter: Demo time — running a baseline run: I'll kick off an evaluation on the "checkout_intent" prompt set.
08:20 Priya Shah: (runs) You can see outputs streaming; the Console shows failing examples on the right, and a distribution plot below. Note there are a couple of mismatched labels — some transcription from our mic showing 'check out' vs 'checkout' — sorry transcript noise there.
09:00 Marisol Vega: Those failing examples — can we export them to a review queue for human relabel?
09:06 Priya Shah: Yes, one-click create a review task, assign to a curator, or export CSV.
09:20 Sofia Ramierez: For our internal process, we'd like the human review to feed back to training data. Is there an export to our dataset registry?
09:28 Priya Shah: Absolutely, export hooks to S3 or BigQuery and we have connectors for common data lakes.
09:40 Ethan Chu: Security question: data at rest encryption, KMS?
09:46 Liam Carter: Redwood supports customer-managed keys with HSM options in Private deployments; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption and SOC2 controls.
09:54 Ethan Chu: Do you have SOC2 and ISO docs?
09:58 Liam Carter: Yes — action item, we'll send SOC2 and our compliance pack.
10:08 Marisol Vega: Another practical: how do we label ambiguous outputs — like multiple acceptable phrasings?
10:16 Priya Shah: Use soft label scoring or multiple acceptable labels; the scoring lambda can return partial credit.
10:28 Sofia Ramierez: Can we store multiple gold labels per prompt?
10:34 Priya Shah: Yes, Console supports multi-gold and weights.
10:40 Liam Carter: Now A/B comparison example: we ran model A vs model B across 2k prompts — here's the delta table — you can click into prompts where the lead changed significantly.
11:05 Marisol Vega: For significance, what assumptions on independence?
11:12 Priya Shah: We use bootstrapped confidence intervals by default; you can choose parametric tests as well.
11:28 Jared Lowe: About automation: can alert policy trigger rollback to previous model automatically?
11:34 Priya Shah: Yes, with Dedicated or Private we can trigger rollback via webhook to your deployment system; for Hosted API we support policy-based routing to fallback model.
11:48 Ethan Chu: Do we get audit logs of who triggered what?
11:52 Asha Patel: Yes, Console has audit logs and RBAC; we can map actions to SSO users.
12:10 Marisol Vega: Ok, costs again — if we run continuous monitoring across 10 prompt sets, will this be expensive?
12:20 Priya Shah: Cost depends on model and frequency — Optimize can recommend cheaper model variants for monitoring and quantization to reduce per-token cost.
12:38 Marisol Vega: Show me an example of Optimize recommending quantization and expected cost savings.
12:44 Priya Shah: (switches) Here's Optimize's recommendation panel — it shows a profile for your workload and suggests int8 quantization plus a caching policy, estimated savings ~40% with <1% quality delta on rank@5.
13:10 Sofia Ramierez: If the quality delta is 1% for rank it might still affect key metrics, how do we validate?
13:18 Priya Shah: You can run an A/B on a holdout cohort before rolling out globally. Also set gating thresholds tied to revenue-critical cohorts.
13:42 Jared Lowe: For pilot, we want Redwood to run baseline on our historical two weeks and surface top 50 failing prompts. What's turnaround?
13:50 Priya Shah: Typically 2-3 business days once data is ingested and access is configured.
14:00 Jared Lowe: Cool. Integration details: we use Okta SSO and private peering.
14:06 Liam Carter: Okta supported for SAML; we'll capture SSO metadata as an action item.
14:18 Marisol Vega: Another ask: tie alerts to Jira tickets automatically for product ops.
14:24 Priya Shah: We have Jira integration for creating issues with failing examples attached.
14:36 Ethan Chu: Any limits on prompt set size?
14:42 Priya Shah: Not really, but we recommend sharding large corpora and using stratified sampling for cost.
14:55 Liam Carter: Let's cover regression alert tuning — you can create policies per-metric, set sensitivity, and add suppression windows to avoid alert storms.
15:12 Marisol Vega: Can we annotate false positives to improve future detection?
15:18 Priya Shah: Yes, feedback loop: mark as false positive and the system will reduce weight of that signal and learn per-prompt behavior.
15:34 Sofia Ramierez: That learning — locally or hosted?
15:40 Priya Shah: Metadata is stored in your tenant; for Private deployments it's in your environment.
15:50 Jared Lowe: Anything about drift alerts causing automated retrain?
15:56 Priya Shah: We don't train models for you, but we can trigger a pipeline webhook to kick off retraining in your infra.
16:08 Liam Carter: Ok wrapping into A/B comparisons — you can attach cohort filters, pick sample size, and get p-values and effect sizes, plus the cost delta.
16:26 Marisol Vega: Demo complete? Any other security concerns?
16:30 Ethan Chu: Data residency — can we keep eval data in EU region?
16:36 Liam Carter: Yes, region pinning is supported for Private and Hosted enterprise with regional isolation.
16:46 Jared Lowe: For the pilot success criteria: detect regressions with >80% precision on top 50 failing prompts and enable automated canary gating that blocked a bad rollout in internal test.
17:02 Asha Patel: We'll capture those success criteria in the runbook.
17:10 Priya Shah: Next steps summary: we'll send SOC2 docs, pilot runbook, and sample ingestion instructions; Acumen shares prompt set and networking contacts.
17:24 Marisol Vega: Sounds good.
17:30 Liam Carter: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.
17:38 Jared Lowe: Thanks all.
17:42 Meeting end.

Note: timestamps above are approximate and the transcript has occasional transcription errors and swapped product names (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes appears as "K V cache", "VPC" shows as "V P C").
